6.6 Peer Review Board (PRB) 

0) ACTIVITIES/ INITIATIVES: 


The Peer Review mechanism was introduced by the Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
(ICAJ) with the setting up of the Peer Review Board in March 2002. The Board is progressing satisfactorily since 
inception and is continuously providing guidance to the members to enhance the efficiency of assurance services 
rendered by them. The main objective of Peer Review is to ensure that in carrying out the assurance service 
assignment, the members of the Institute (a) comply with Technical, Professional and Ethical Standards as 
applicable including other regulatory requirements thereto and (b) have in place proper systems including 
documentation thereof, to amply demonstrate the quality of the assurance services. The Peer Review is conducted 
of a Practice Unit by an independent evaluator known as a Peer Reviewer. 


e Recognition of Peer Review by Regulators: 
The Peer Reviewed firms are given recognition even by the regulators as stated below: - 


> SEBI, with effect from April l, 20l0, has made it mandatory for the listed entities, that limited 
review/statutory audit reports submitted to the concerned stock exchanges shall be given only by those 
auditors who have subjected themselves to peer review process and who hold a valid certificate issued 


24 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEC.4] 


by the ‘Peer Review Board’ of the Institute. 


> The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C & AG) has revised the Policy of Empanelment of CA 
Firms/LLPs and appointment of auditors of Companies under Section 39(5) and 39(7) of the 
Companies Act 20l3 and of Statutory Corporations/Autonomous Bodies as per the provisions of their 
respective Acts. A maximum of 25 points allotted to firms which hold a Peer Review Certificate on the 
date of making an application for empanelment. 


e Peer Review of Practice Units: 


The Peer Review Board has considered and issued 426 Peer Review Certificates to the Practice Units during 
the period 0.04.2024-3.05.2025. As on 3.05.2025, a total of 6859 Practice Units held valid Peer Review 
Certificate.

(II) Peer Review Mandate-Roll Out Implementation 


e Applicability of Phase II of the Peer Review Mandate 


The second phase of the mandate was earlier applicable w.e.f April l, 2023 for the Practice Units which 
propose to undertake Statutory Audit of unlisted public companies having paid-up capital of not less than 
rupees 500 crores or having annual turnover of not less than rupees l000 crores or having, in aggregate, 
outstanding loans, debentures and deposits of not less than rupees 500 crores as on the 3lst March of 
immediately preceding financial year OR Practice units rendering attestation services and having 5 or more 
partners. The Council initially decided to defer the applicability of the second phase of the mandate by three 
months to be made effective from July l, 2023. This was later extended upto 3l‘t March 2024. Then, grace 
period was allowed for another 3 months. Phase II of the mandate was made applicable from July |, 2024. 


e Deferment of Phase III of the Peer Review Mandate 


The third phase of the mandate was earlier applicable w.e.f April l, 2024 for the Practice Units which have 
raised funds from public or banks or financial institutions of over Fifty Crores rupees during the period under 
review or of any body corporate including trusts which are covered under public interest entities OR Practice 
units rendering attestation services and having 4 or more partners. The Council initially decided to defer the 
applicability of the third phase of the mandate by nine months to be made effective from January |, 2025. This 
was further extended by six months to be made applicable from July l, 2025. 


e Deferment of Phase IV of the Peer Review Mandate 


The third phase of the mandate was earlier applicable w.e.f April l, 2025 for the Practice Units which propose 
to undertake audits of branches of Public Sector Banks OR Practice units rendering attestation services and 
having 3 or more partners.The Council initially decided to defer the applicability of the fourth phase of the 
mandate by nine months to be made effective from January |, 2026. 


e Clarifications/FAQs on the issues arising out of the Peer Review Mandate 


Peer Review Board has issued clarifications/FAQs on the various issues arising out of the Peer Review 
Mandate. These clarifications/FAQs are hosted at http://resource.cdn.icai.org/8357]prb67450.pdf.

(IV) Peer Review Portal: 


The Peer Review Board is developing a dedicated web portal to streamline and enhance its peer review process. 
This innovative platform will centralize all review activities, from submission of application to decision-making. 
By leveraging advanced technology, we aim to improve efficiency, transparency and effectiveness of peer review

(V) Other Initiatives: 


The Board has been making continuous efforts to make the Peer Review mechanism more effective. The level of 
awareness created during the last 23 years has indeed brought about an overall improvement in the quality of 
assurance services rendered by the members. A comprehensive all-encompassing approach has been followed to 
create an enabling eco-system including by: 


e Developing sufficient and competent resources for review; 
e Improvising the quality of peer reviews; and 


e Initiating steps to make increased use of technology in the peer review process so as to effectively overcome 
capacity constraints. 


6.7 Taxation Audits Quality Review Board (TAQRB) 

ACTIVITIES/ INITIATIVES: 

The Taxation Audits Quality Review Board was constituted by the Institute in the year 208 in order to improve 
the reporting of compliances under various taxation laws (both Direct as well as Indirect). It is envisaged that the 
reviews carried out by the Board, will ensure that the members will exercise greater diligence while certifying the 


various reports prescribed under direct and indirect taxation and in the long-run would improve the overall 
reporting and certification done by them.

Audit.

identified for the purpose of creating awareness amongst the members.

To enhance operational efficiency and streamline processes, the Board has developed a web portal 
(taqrb.icai.org). This portal serves as a centralized repository for TAQRB reports, minutes, and case follow- 
ups, ensuring seamless documentation and accessibility. Moreover, the system automates key workflows 
across various levels (TR, TAQRG, and TAQRB), including case allocation, report submissions, and real- 
time tracking of progress. By integrating automation, the portal enhances transparency, improves 
coordination, and accelerates decision-making, reinforcing TAQRB’s commitment to efficiency and digital 
transformation. The steps taken above are expected to improvise the quality of tax audit conducted by the 
members. 


6.8 Direct Taxes Committee (DTC) 


The Direct Taxes Committee (DTC) of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is a key committee 
dedicated to matters related to direct taxation. It actively engages with the Government, the Central Board of Direct 
Taxes (CBDT), and other relevant forums by making representations on legislative amendments and pressing 
issues concerning direct taxes. A primary focus of the Committee is to enhance the knowledge and skills of ICAI 
members in direct taxation through the publication of new materials, updates to existing resources, and the 
organization of seminars, webinars, and conferences.

6.9 Sustainability Reporting Standards Board (SRSB) 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has a strong tradition of service to the country towards 
sustainable as well as economic development. ICAI strives to bring sustainability reporting and thinking within 
mainstream business practices both in the public and private sectors. ICAI through SRSB is taking proactive steps 
to not only identify and develop opportunities for Chartered Accountants in Sustainability domain but also to 
enhance knowledge, upskill and train members by conducting workshops, seminars, and certificate course, publish 
technical literature on various important topics within the sustainability domain. Further, in its endeavor to promote 
sustainability ecosystem in the country which would lead to greener low-carbon economy, the Institute is working 
on two crucial aspects. Firstly, to promote compliance with existing sustainability related disclosure requirements. 
Secondly, to strengthen assurance framework to build a solid bridge between sustainability related risks and 
corporate reporting.

6.0 Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board 


The Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board (I& VSB) of ICAI has been constituted in the year 2024-2025 to act 
as an instrument for the empowerment of the profession and aims to facilitate a fair corporate regime with the best 
global practices in the sphere of Insolvency and Valuation. Also, the Board has been formed to focus on 
advancement of activities for formulation, implementation and recognition of ICAI Valuation Standards 208. The 
Insolvency & Valuation Standard Board (I&VSB) plays a crucial role in maintaining financial stability by 
establishing and promoting transparent and consistent standards in the fields of insolvency and valuation.

(II) Publications released by Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board, ICAI 


White Paper on International Convention on Insolvency Resolution and Valuation - RESOLVE-2024- 
The Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board (I& VSB) of ICAI, in collaboration with IBBI, hosted the 
International Convention on Insolvency Resolution and Valuation—RESOLVE 2024—on July 2-3, 2024, 
in New Delhi. The event gathered global experts to discuss challenges and promote alignment of Indian 
insolvency practices with international standards. Featuring nine technical sessions and seven panel 
discussions, the convention focused on enhancing the insolvency framework. A White Paper summarizing key 
insights, issues, and recommendations was prepared to guide improvements in the Insolvency and Bankruptcy 
Code, 206. 


Issues and Recommendations arising out of the discussions at International Convention on Insolvency 
Resolution and Valuation - RESOLVE 2024- On the basis of the detailed discussions at the Convention, the 
Board published a document specifically focusing on the Issues and Recommendations arising from the 
deliberations during RESOLVE-2024. This document will help the Regulators, Policy Makers, Judiciary and 
other stakeholders in taking further actions and in plugging the gaps and providing solutions. Further, it will 
provide valuable insights to all the stakeholders including Insolvency Professionals and Registered Valuers 
and serve as important resource for Insolvency Professionals and Valuers, guiding them towards improved 
practices in insolvency resolution and valuation. 


Judicial Pronouncements under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 Series-5- This publication is a 
part of an ongoing series aimed at enhancing awareness and understanding of the evolving judicial 
interpretations of the IBC framework. This highlights summary of landmark rulings by the Supreme Court, 
High Court, NCLAT, and NCLT, which have clarified provisions, resolved ambiguities, and strengthened the 
legal framework for insolvency resolution. Through this series, the I & VSB equips stakeholders with 
practical insights into procedural intricacies, fostering greater expertise and efficiency in insolvency resolution 
practices. 


A Study on the Efficacy of IBC, 206 in meeting deadlines and maximizing value during the Corporate 
Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)- This research study provides an analysis of delays in the Corporate 
Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), their impact on asset realization values, and the prevalence of defunct 
companies under CIRP. By examining these factors and offering actionable recommendations, the study aims 
to provide as a guide towards enhancing the efficiency and efficacy of insolvency proceedings, fostering a 
more robust resolution framework in India. 


Educational Material on ICAI Valuation Standard 302- Intangible Assets- This Educational Material 
aims to provide clarity and guidance on the complex process of valuing intangible assets, which often form a 
significant part of a company's value. This publication offers practical insights, case studies, and detailed 
guidance on valuation practices in accordance with ICAI Valuation Standards 208. It supports consistent and 
uniform practices across India and contributes to enhancing the efficiency and expertise of valuers, ultimately 
fostering transparency and stability in financial markets. 


Summary of Amendments in Regulations under The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 (Revised 
February 2025 Edition)- This publication aims to provide a concise overview of key regulatory updates to 
the IBC framework introduced in 2023 and 2024. These amendments, addressing various aspects such as 
insolvency professionals, information utilities, corporate insolvency, liquidation, and inspection processes, are 
designed to enhance the Code's efficiency and implementation. Notable changes include allowing the 
committee of creditors to approve audits during resolution processes, mandating separate bank accounts for 
real estate projects, revising fees for creditor representatives, and ensuring timely committee meetings. 


Unicorns, Soonicorns, and the Myth of Valuation - A Critical Examination of Startup Growth and 
Sustainability - Series - This booklet delves into the dynamic world of startups, exploring their valuation 
paradigms from ideation to unicorn status. With India emerging as a global hub for innovation, this booklet 
examines the factors influencing startup valuations, including the challenges posed by untested products, 
uncertain growth projections, and intangible assets. The booklet features real world examples from prominent 


[भाग [--खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 223 


companies like Swiggy, Flipkart, and Ola, illustrating their distinct valuation journeys and strategic decisions 
that have defined their paths to success. 


e Frequently Asked Questions on The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 (Revised February 2025 
Edition)- This publication is brought by I & VSB of ICAI in collaboration with Insolvency and Bankruptcy 
Board of India. The publication has been designed in a question-and-answer format which comprehensively 
covers questions to assist our members and other stakeholders to have conceptual clarity on the 
various aspects of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206. Further appropriate case laws have been included 
so as to help in understanding the provisions under the Code clearly and also know about the practical aspects. 


e Handbook on Do's and Don'ts for IPs under The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 (Revised 
February 2025 Edition)- This handbook guides Insolvency Professionals (IPs) on their roles, responsibilities, 
and regulatory compliance under the IBC and IBBI Code of Conduct. It helps IPs understand and fulfill their 
duties with due diligence, reflecting recent amendments and judicial rulings on best practices and restrictions 
to ensure effective and compliant insolvency resolution. 


e Handbook on Claims under The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 (Revised February 2025 
Edition- This revised publication offers detailed guidance on the submission, admission, verification, and 
management of claims under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), covering processes like CIRP and 
liquidation. It includes provisions, timelines, forms, FAQs, and case laws to help insolvency professionals 
handle claims efficiently and compliantly. The update reflects recent amendments and judicial rulings on 
claim inclusions and acceptance deadlines. 


e Handbook on Resolution Plan under The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206 (Revised February 
2025 Edition)- This revised Handbook guides professionals on the complex aspects of Resolution Plans under 
the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). It details the submission and approval processes, mandatory 
contents, and the invitation of expressions of interest from resolution applicants. The updated edition 
incorporates recent amendments and judicial rulings, providing Insolvency Professionals with essential 
insights for efficient insolvency resolution in India. 


e Question Bank on IBBI Limited Insolvency Examination (Revised February 2025 Edition)-The Question 
Bank aims to assist professionals in preparing for the Limited Insolvency Examination conducted by the IBBI. 
This examination is a key requirement for becoming an Insolvency Professional, a vital role in the insolvency 
and bankruptcy resolution process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 20l6. This revised edition 
incorporates amendments and updates since its last edition, ensuring alignment with the latest regulatory 
changes. This publication serves as a practical and handy resource to support aspiring insolvency 
professionals in understanding the Code and excelling in their professional journey. Due to various 
amendments and changes, this publication has been revised. 


e Background Material for the Certificate Course on The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 206- The 
Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board (I&VSB) of ICAI has released Background Material for the 
Certificate Course on the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 20l6. This resource helps participants 
understand insolvency laws, resolution processes, and regulations, aiding them in exam preparation. It covers 
key topics like resolution planning, creditor meetings, and bid evaluation, ensuring Insolvency Professionals 
maintain transparency and legal compliance. The initiative aims to develop skilled professionals and 
strengthen trust in the financial system. 


(IIT) Development of ICAI Valuation Standards for other two assets class i.e., “Plant & Machinery” and 
“Land & Building” in addition to “Securities or Financial Assets” 


The Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board is developing Valuation Standards for Land & Building, Plant & 
Machinery, and Securities & Financial Assets. Drafts have been prepared for Plant, Machinery and Equipment, Real 
Property Interest, and Development Property, with the formulation process currently underway.

2024” held on 2® - ]3% July 2024 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi 


The Insolvency & Valuation Standards Board of ICAI organized the second edition of RESOLVE-2024: An

6.l Committee on International Taxation 


The Committee on International Taxation (CITAX) was previously merged with the Direct Taxes Committee in the 
year 2023-24. However, with the introduction of the Income-tax Bill, 2025, the scope of work in both Direct Taxes 
and International Taxation would expand significantly. Additionally, with the diploma course on international 
taxation and certification course on UAE Corporate tax running concurrently in either physical or virtual mode, 
manifold publications, and a number of seminars, conferences etc. related to direct taxes and international taxation, 
there is a need for focus on both domains. In view of this, International Taxation Committee has been demerged 


[भाग Il—ave 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 225 


from Direct Taxes Committee for the year 2025-26. The Committee on International Taxation plays a vital role in 
addressing matters related to international tax laws and policies. It examines tax laws, rules, regulations, circulars, 
and notifications issued by the Government pertaining to international taxation and submits suitable suggestions 
through detailed memoranda. It represents on OECD/UN papers, promotes research, organizes seminars and study 
tours, publishes technical material, and coordinates with overseas bodies, aiming to enhance member knowledge in 
international taxation.

As part of its ongoing efforts to enhance the professional knowledge and competencies of ICAI members, the

6.2 Corporate Laws and Corporate Governance Committee (CL&CGC) 


The Corporate Laws & Corporate Governance Committee (CL&CGC) is to empower the profession and promote a 
fair corporate regime through global best practices. The Committee actively strengthens the regulatory framework 
by engaging with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and providing regular representations and suggestions to 
enhance stakeholders experience and on matters pertaining to the Companies Act 203. With a focus on knowledge 
enhancement, the Committee strives to empower members of the Institute to stay current on corporate laws, 
enabling them to navigate the evolving landscape of corporate governance effectively. 


Significant Achievements and Initiatives 


(I) Suggestions on SEBI Consultation Paper 

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) released a Consultation Paper on 7" February 2025, 
concerning secretarial compliance reports, appointment of auditors, and related party transactions (RPTs) of 
listed entities. The Committee reviewed the consultation paper, which proposes amendments to the SEBI 
(LODR) Regulations, aimed at enhancing transparency based on Advisory Committee on Listing Obligations 
and Disclosures (ACLOD) recommendations. Accordingly, the Committee submitted its suggestions to SEBI. 


(II) Suggestions on the Income-tax Bill, 2025 

In response to a request from the MCA, the ICAI submitted its comments on provisions under the Companies 
Act, 20I3 relevant to the Income-tax Bill, 2025. Detailed suggestions finalized after extensive deliberations and 
reviewed by an expert group were forwarded for onward submission to the Hon’ble Select Committee of the 
Lok Sabha.

6.3 Committee on Commercial Laws, Economic Advisory & NPO Cooperative (CCLEA&NPO) 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is committed to shaping the future of the accountancy 
profession by promoting excellence and acting as a trusted partner within the financial ecosystem. The Committee 
on Commercial Laws, Economic Advisory & NPO Cooperative (CCLEANC) of ICAI plays a vital role in 
equipping Chartered Accountants with in-depth knowledge and practical expertise across commercial laws, 
economic advisory, and the governance of Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs) and cooperatives. The Committee 
contributes to nation-building by empowering members to serve as reliable advisors in areas such as corporate 
governance, regulatory compliance, and dispute resolution. To strengthen professional capabilities, the Committee 
develops high-quality publications, conducts focused research, and utilizes digital platforms to disseminate 
knowledge. It regularly provides members with monthly updates, handbooks, and FAQs tailored to key laws and 
regulatory developments. Moreover, the Committee engages proactively with regulators and policymakers, 
representing the profession’s interests and advocating for reforms that promote transparency and good governance. 
Through these initiatives, CCLEANC enables Chartered Accountants to confidently address emerging challenges, 
drive economic growth, and leverage new opportunities in a dynamic global landscape.

6.5 Ethical Standards Board (ESB) 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India has constituted the Ethical Standards Board as the designated 
standard-setting authority for ethical governance within the profession. The Board is vested with the mandate to 
develop and implement ethical standards and other authoritative pronouncements applicable to Chartered 
Accountants. In fulfilling its mandate, the Board endeavours to evolve a dynamic and contemporary Code of Ethics 
and ethical framework for members, while upholding the time-honoured principles of excellence, independence, 
and integrity, thereby safeguarding the dignity and interests of the members. The objective of the Ethical Standards 
Board is to formulate and promulgate ethical standards for Chartered Accountants that align with internationally 
recognized best practices, subject to compliance with applicable domestic laws. Through this alignment, the Board 
aims to enhance the quality, consistency, and reliability of services rendered by Chartered Accountants, thereby 
reinforcing public confidence and trust in the profession. 


Since its inception, the Board has diligently engaged in establishing and maintaining standards that regulate the 
professional conduct and qualification of ICAI members. In addition to its core responsibilities, the Board actively 
undertakes initiatives aimed at augmenting members’ professional competitiveness and dynamism. Moreover, the 
Board administers a grievance redressal mechanism concerning instances of unjustified removal of members as 
auditors. This function serves as a protective measure to uphold the independence of members, ensuring that those 
adversely affected by unwarranted auditor removals have access to equitable recourse and justice. 


(D Significant Achievements

for awareness at all Branches/Regional Councils in the month of October on this occasion. Special edition 
of CA Journal for October Month dedicated to theme of Ethics was issued. Ethics quiz and string of other 
measures for dissemination of ethics among members were organized.

6.6 Digital Accounting and Assurance Board (DAAB) 


The Digital Accounting and Assurance Board (DAAB) traces its roots to the year 2000, when ICAI established the 
Committee on Information Technology (CIT) to spearhead the profession’s IT initiatives. In its first decade, CIT 
focused on raising IT awareness, introducing the Information Systems Audit (ISA) course, and building basic 
technology infrastructure for members. In 2009, the committee broadened the scope by including forensic 
accounting, XBRL implementation, e-learning, and greater technology integration into audit practices. Recognizing 
the accelerating digital transformation in finance, ICAI reconstituted this committee as the Digital Accounting and 
Assurance Board (DAAB) in 209, with an expanded mandate covering digital competencies, forensic standards, 
blockchain, AI, and global partnerships. This evolution over two decades laid the groundwork for a proactive body 
attuned to the emerging challenges and opportunities of the digital era. 


(I) Key Milestones and Initiatives 


e DISA Launches and Upgrades: The journey began with the launch of the Post-Qualification course on 
Information Systems Audit (ISA) in 2000, which provided Chartered Accountants specialized training in IT 
auditing. This program later, undergone multiple syllabus revisions (DISA .0, 2.0, 3.0) to keep pace with 
technological advances. Over the years, DISA gained formal recognition from regulators notably the 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and market authorities enabling DISA-qualified members to conduct bank 
system audits as experts. Today, DAAB is in the process of rolling out DISA 4.0, a comprehensive upgrade 
that will incorporate cybersecurity frameworks, data privacy (DPDP Act) compliance, regulatory 
technology (RegTech), and other emerging areas into the curriculum. 


e Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection (FAFD) Course: Recognizing the growing need for forensic 
expertise, ICAI launched the Certificate Course on Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection (FAFD) in 
2009, equipping members with investigative skills supported by hands-on training through forensic labs, 
including one established in Noida in 207. As the field evolved, DAAB continually upgraded the course— 
most notably aligning it in 2023 with ICAI’s world-first Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards 
(FAIS), now mandatory for forensic assignments. In 2024, DAAB initiated the course's transition into a full- 
fledged Diploma in Forensic Investigation (DFI), which received initial approval from the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs and is set for public exposure before final clearance—marking a major step in advancing 
formal forensic education. 


e __ Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS): A landmark achievement of the DAAB era 
has been the development of Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS) — a comprehensive 
framework to guide practitioners in forensic accounting engagements. Released in series (totalling 20 
individual standards and 3 overarching documents) and refined through expert input, the FAIS were 
officially issued with mandatory implementation from 2023 onwards. These standards cover the entire 
gamut of forensic accounting, from evidence collection and analysis to reporting, and serve as a definitive 
benchmark for quality and consistency in forensic services undertaken by chartered accountants. 


e _ Digital Competency Maturity Model (DCMM): To help the profession assess and improve its adoption 
of technology, the Board developed the Digital Competency Maturity Model (DCMM) Version | and in 
209, DCMM 2.0, its implementation guide and a tool was released which provides a structured model with 
defined levels and an implementation guide for firms to evaluate their digital capabilities. Further, it was 
made part of Peer review also. By benchmarking areas such as IT infrastructure, software tools, process 
automation, and digital skills, DCMM has enabled audit firms (especially small and medium practices) to 
identify gaps and roadmaps for digital transformation. The model’s relevance has extended beyond India — it 
has been showcased in international forums and adapted by global accounting groups as a tool for enhancing 
digital practices in the accounting profession. 


e International Outreach : From its early years, DAAB has extended its impact internationally. In the mid- 
2000s, ICAI’s IT Committee began delivering ISA courses in Sri Lanka and Nepal, supported by MoUs 
with ICASL and ICAN. These collaborations later expanded to include forensic accounting training. By 
2025, ICASL expressed interest in adopting ICAI’s forensic standards, reflecting their global relevance. 
DAAB has also conducted virtual DISA classes for professionals in both countries and hosted international 
participants in its programs. A key example was the customized FAFD training for Bank of Bhutan auditors 
in October 2024. These efforts have strengthened ICAI’s global standing in digital accounting and 
assurance. 


[भाग ता--खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 233 


e Government and Regulatory Collaborations : Over its 25-year journey, DAAB has played a pivotal 
role in integrating digital audit and forensic practices into governance through close collaboration with 
government bodies and regulators. Key milestones include early engagement with the CAG to introduce IS 
audit in public audits and RBI’s recognition of the DISA qualification for statutory bank IS audits. More 
recently, DAAB has supported law enforcement by training agencies like the Gujarat Police Economic 
Offences Wing and recommending ICAI’s forensic standards. In 2024, the Board signed MoUs with 
Rashtriya Raksha University and NFSU to collaborate on cybersecurity, AI, and forensic research. DAAB 
has also conducted specialized training for agencies such as SFIO, CBI, CAG, ICLS Academy, DGGI, and 
major PSUs like SBI, BOB, HPCL, and IOCL—teinforcing its role as a trusted advisor in advancing 
financial transparency and digital governance.

In its 25th year, DAAB continued to drive innovation and capacity-building through several high-impact initiatives, 
aligning with its long-term strategic goals: 


° Upgrading Qualifications 


In 2024-25, DAAB prioritized upgrading ICAI’s post-qualification courses to equip members with cutting-edge 
skills. The DISA program is being upgraded to Version 4.0 with enhanced content on cybersecurity, DPDP Act 
compliance, RegTech, and IT governance. Exam frequency has been increased to allow faster course 
completion. The FAFD course is being elevated to a Diploma in Forensic Investigation (DFI), with a proposal 
submitted to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Additionally, a new “DISA+” refresher course is being 
developed to keep DISA alumni updated on emerging trends in IT audit and technology. 


e Conferences and Thought Leadership: 


In 2024-25, DAAB organized several flagship conferences to promote thought leadership in digital accounting 
and assurance. Key events included Future Proof Forensics in Mumbai, a two-day summit on financial fraud 
investigation with 35+ participants from banks, regulators, and enforcement agencies; Pragyotsav-2024 in 
Jaipur, a national conference on internal audit and technology attended by 2,000 professionals and inaugurated 
by the Hon’ble Vice President of India; and Gyan se Vigyan in Belagavi, focused on digital transformation in 
accountancy with 476 participants. Looking ahead, DAAB has announced the Digital Transformation (Dx) 
Finance Summit 2025 in Hyderabad, themed “Fortifying Finance: Forensics, Cybersecurity & Digital Trust,” 
targeting top finance and tech leaders to explore cutting-edge developments in AI, blockchain, cyber 
governance, and ICAI’s forensic standards.

conducted a specialized Financial Crime Investigation training for 64 officers of the Gujarat Police’s Economic

(IID) Membership Growth

appetite among chartered accountants for upskilling in high-demand areas. The ever-increasing number of DISA 
and FAFD alumni demonstrates how the Board’s efforts have strengthened the profession’s collective capability to 
perform IT audits, cybersecurity assessments, forensic investigations, and other technology-driven services. 


(IV) Collaborations and Outreach 


The Digital Accounting and Assurance Board (DAAB) of ICAI, celebrating its 25-year journey from an IT 
Committee in 2000 to a leading board in 2025, has played a key role in advancing digital excellence in the 
profession. Through collaborations with global bodies like ISACA, ICASL, and Hyperledger, DAAB has enriched 
education in information systems audit, forensics, and blockchain. Its standards are being adopted internationally, 
and its partnership in launching EFAA’s global competency model highlights its leadership. DAAB’s initiatives 
have empowered thousands of CAs and strengthened public trust in the profession’s digital readiness. Looking 
ahead, ICAI aims to build on this legacy through continued innovation and global collaboration.

73 COMMITTEE FOR AGGREGATION OF CA FIRMS 


The Committee for Aggregation of CA Firms (CACAF), constituted in 2024-2025 by the ICAI, stands at the 
forefront of reshaping the landscape for CA firms in India. Tasked with a pivotal role, CACAF’s vision is driven 
by a commitment to conduct an exhaustive review and revision of various existing guidelines pertaining to CA 
firms, ensuring they are not only relevant but also adaptive to the continuously evolving professional and 
regulatory landscape thereby enhancing their operational efficacy and global competitiveness. CACAF seeks to 
empower CA firms to expand their expertise, scale operations and navigate the dynamic professional landscape 
effectively. The Committee's strategic initiatives are designed to streamline processes, reduce policy and 
procedural impediments and cultivate an ecosystem of resilience and excellence. Through stakeholder engagement, 
capacity building and continuous feedback, CACAF ensures that CA firms are well-equipped to thrive in an 
increasingly competitive and evolving global market. 


(D) Significant Achievements 
e Revision of the ICAI (Merger & Demerger of CA Firms) Guidelines 2024: 


The Committee has made concerted efforts in reviewing and revising the Merger and Demerger Guidelines. 
Comprehensive efforts have been made, ranging from conducting surveys to the exposure draft of the revised 
guidelines, interactive brainstorming sessions with CA Firms to threadbare discussions in various meetings of 
the Committee. The ICAI (Merger & Demerger of CA Firms) Guidelines, 2024 were approved in July 2024 and 
have been notified in the Gazette of India. It has been endeavoured to streamline the guidelines both at policy 
and procedural levels. 


e Introduction of the ICAI (Aggregation of LLPs) Guidelines 2024: 


The Committee has also brought a set of new guidelines for Aggregation of the Indian CA Firms. It basically 
provides an opportunity for an LLP, Indian CA Firm to be a partner with another LLP, a CA Firm. This 
particular concept among LLPs will serve as a vital tool for strategic growth. By these guidelines, firms can 
significantly expand their capabilities, broaden their market presence, and achieve substantial operational 
efficiencies. This strategic move allows them to leverage combined resources, diversify service offerings and 
enhance competitive advantages, ultimately driving long-term success and sustainability in an increasingly 
competitive landscape. The ICAI (Aggregation of LLPs) Guidelines, 2024 were approved in July 2024 and 
have been notified in the Gazette of India. 


e Draft Guidelines for Overseas Network: 


In alignment with ICAI's vision of expanding India's footprint on the global stage, the Draft Guidelines for 
Overseas Network is under finalization. These guidelines aim to establish a structured and regulated pathway 
for networking and collaboration. This initiative is designed to foster global connectivity, enhance professional 
opportunities for Indian CA firms, uphold the integrity and quality of services delivered as well as to support 
the evolving needs of the profession in an interconnected world.

7.5 Committee on MSME & Start-up 


The Committee on MSME and Startup is a non-standing committee of the ICAI, established to address the critical 
needs of the MSME and Startup sectors in India. Its primary objective is to enhance capacity through the 
development of sustainable frameworks tailored specifically for these sectors. By focusing on training, advocacy, 
and policy recommendations, the committee aims to bolster the growth and resilience of Indian MSMEs and 
startups, thereby fostering a conducive environment for entrepreneurship and economic development. 


(I) Initiatives of the Committee on MSME & Startup, ICAI 


To enhance the capacity building measures of MSME & Startups, the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
(ICAJ) through the Committee on MSME & Start-up launched various initiatives on MSME & Start-up. 


e ICAI Startup Manthan- The Committee on MSME & Start-up organized ICAI Startup Manthan on [7॥ 
January 2025 at Jio World Centre, BKC, Mumbai. This program brings together thought leaders, investors, 
entrepreneurs, and key stakeholders in the startup ecosystem to discuss pertinent issues and share valuable 
insights. The event covered Government ecosystem, new avenues, funding challenges, exit strategies along 
with felicitation from Asia & India book of records for ICAI MSME & Startup yatra 2024. 


e Startup Sphere 2024- The Committee on MSME & Startup, along with related ICAI directorates, 
organized the three-day Startup Sphere 2024 event in Bengaluru from June 27-29, 2024, themed “Startup 
Synergy: Collaborate, Create, Conquer.” The event showcased government support, funding sources, startup 
valuation, digital marketing, and celebrated International MSME Day. It brought together founders,

and part of ICAI’s “Hamara Sankalp Viksit Bharat” initiative, focused on building a sustainable Indian

of ProScaler.ai and Founder of SaffronStays, who shared their startup journeys. The series served as a 
valuable knowledge-sharing platform for aspiring entrepreneurs and stakeholders in the startup ecosystem.

during January 2025.

members offering consultancy in areas like corporate laws, valuation, and indirect tax, and showcasing CA- 
led startup success stories to inspire others. The portal currently has over 200 startups, 78 investors, and 269 
mentors registered, fostering collaboration and growth within the startup ecosystem.

7.6 Committee on Promoting Work Life Balance 


The Committee on Promoting Work-Life Balance is a newly constituted in the Council Year 2025-26, body with 
the vision to empower ICAI stakeholders to harmonize their professional commitments along with personal well- 
being. The Committee is committed to nurturing a healthy work-life balance, encouraging sustainable career 
growth, and strengthening ICAI’s standing as a globally recognized leader in the accountancy profession. Through 
this endeavor, the Committee aspires to cultivate not only enhanced professional excellence but also a more 
fulfilling quality of life. 


(I) Details of Programmes undertaken by the Committee as part to promote Wellness 


To commemorate World Laughter Day on 470 May, 2025, the Committee hosted a lively and engaging celebration 
across ICAI’s Regional Offices and Branches nationwide. Chartered Accountants from all corners of the country— 
from Jammu & Kashmir in the North to Trivandrum in the South, and from Dibrugarh in the East to Bhuj in the 
West—participated with enthusiasm and unity. Many Chartered Accountants showcased their talents through 
engaging performances such as mimicry and stand-up comedy in various branches. The event highlighted the 
uplifting power of laughter as a natural remedy for stress, fostering a sense of community and well-being among 
members. 


(II) Webcast organized by the Committee to highlight the significance of physical and mental health as a key 
component of Promoting Work Life Balance 


In May 2025, the Committee organized a series of wellness-focused webinars for Chartered Accountants, covering 
diverse aspects of personal and professional well-being. Topics included redefining fitness "From Calculators to 
Kettlebells", life planning and balance, Work and Wellbeing:", mental resilience "Stronger Minds, Sharper 
Numbers" and relationship building beyond the workplace "Nurturing Connections" etc. 


7.7 Continuing Professional Education Committee (CPEC) 


The Profession of Chartered Accountancy plays a critical role in enhancing transparency, ensuring compliance, and 
supporting effective decision-making across both public and private sectors. This profession represents foundation 
of financial integrity and strategic advisory within the global business environment. Chartered Accountants (CAs) 
are distinguished by their rigorous education, comprehensive professional training, and unwavering adherence to 
ethical and regulatory standards. Their expertise spans financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and business advisory 
services, making them integral to sound financial governance. ICAI through its Continuing Professional Education 
Committee, consistently strives to provide meaningful learning opportunities for its members. Continuing 
Professional Education (CPE) is not merely a mandatory requirement but a strategic investment in the professional 
growth of Chartered Accountants. It yields substantial returns in the form of enhanced technical proficiency, 


[भाग Wave 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 247 


broader professional networks, and the confidence to address emerging complexities in the financial landscape. In a 
rapidly evolving business and regulatory environment—marked by the introduction of new accounting standards, 
dynamic compliance frameworks, and technological advancements—staying informed and up to date is essential. 
The CPE Committee of ICAI equips members with the necessary knowledge and tools to adapt to these changes 
effectively. By doing so, it empowers Chartered Accountants to consistently deliver value to their clients and 
organizations, upholding the highest standards of professional competence and integrity. Furthermore, a strong 
emphasis on continuous professional development ensures that Chartered Accountants remain current with 
evolving regulations, technologies, and business practices. 


(D Significant Achievements and Initiatives 


e Organisation of National Level Programmes 


CPE Committee organised a 2-day National CA Conference 2024 on the theme "समृद्धि: Fostering Growth, 
Fuelling Success" hosted by Bhubaneswar Branch of EIRC of ICAI. The Conference was inaugurated by the 
Chief Guest, then Governor of RBI & Guest of Honour, CMD GAIL (India) in presence of the then President, 
ICAI in presence of other dignitaries. More than 250 delegates from across the Nation has attended this 
historic Conference. The sessions were taken by the galaxy of star speakers who enriched the participants with 
an illuminating and educative experience. In the Valedictory Ceremony, Deputy Chief Minister of Odisha was 
Chief Guest along with CMD of NALCO, were present. 


e Focus on quality and availability of CPE Programmes across globe and to enhance quality of CPE 
Programmes in terms of CPE Learning & Delivery Mechanism 


To enhance the quality and relevance of CPE programmes, the CPE Committee of ICAI (CPEC) has 
strengthened its regulatory framework with improved topic selection, faculty engagement, and programme 
structuring. A stricter monitoring system ensures compliance by CPE Organising Units (POUs), promoting 
accountability and continual improvement. CPEC has also introduced a faculty review and feedback 
mechanism to assess teaching effectiveness and build a strong pool of competent faculty. The CPE Portal now 
features an advanced faculty search tool for better faculty selection. Additionally, CPEC provides financial 
support to Regional Councils, Branches, and Study Chapters to promote accessible, high-quality learning across 
India. 


e सर्व-सु्रभ CPE Programme - To reach out to the Member of ICAI at remotest place of country for 
dissemination of knowledge 


With the objective of promoting the ICAI brand, the CPE Committee has undertaken a new initiative this year 
aimed at reaching even the remotest members of ICAI across the country for effective dissemination of 


knowledge. This initiative has been themed as 'सर्व-सुलभ — CPE Programme' and it ensures for the effective 
transmission of knowledge to every ICAI member, regardless of their location. 


e New format of CPE Calendar of topics for 2025-26 


The CPE Committee revises the CPE Calendar of topics every year for organizing CPE Programmes through its 
CPE POUs. This year, the Chairman of the CPE Committee has proposed a revamp of the CPE Calendar, 
suggesting a new format and a more visually appealing design to enhance its presentation. In line with above, 
this year, the CPE Calendar has been featured in three comprehensive parts i.e Part A outlines standard 
programme structures focused on current thrust areas within the professional landscape. Part B offers a module- 
wise learning framework, complete with defined CPE hours and Part C presents an extensive list of suggested 
topics relevant to Chartered Accountancy professionals. 


e Organizing of “Train the Trainers” and “Faculty Development Programmes” for development of 
faculty database by CPE Committee and to have their regular monitoring and review system 


With the objective of building a nationwide pool of skilled and effective faculty members, the CPE Committee 
has initiated and proposed “Train the Trainer” programmes across the country. These programmes are designed 
to equip potential and existing faculty members with the necessary tools and techniques to deliver high-quality 
learning experiences during CPE sessions. The “Train the Trainer’ initiative serves as a strategic approach to 
enhance the pedagogical capabilities of subject matter experts. It focuses on key areas such as effective teaching 
methodologies, fostering inclusive and engaging learning environments, improving communication and 
presentation skills, and mastering the art of public speaking. Through this initiative, the CPE Committee aims to 
ensure that faculties are not only experts in their subject areas but are also proficient in delivering knowledge in 
a professional, impactful, and learner-centric manner.

e Identification of new CPE POUs to be opened in all Districts/Tehsils in India to connect and facilitate 
the members in mofussil/remote areas to undergo CPE activities 


The CPE Committee as per its Action Plan 2025-26 proposed to reach to l000+ POUs in all 
States/Districts/Tehsils (Mofussil Areas) in India to facilitate CPE learning to all members of the ICAI residing 
in far flung areas of the country. The Committee is keen in expanding its strong Network base of 696 POUs 
vide opening of CPE POUs in all Districts/Tehsils in India to Connect and facilitate the members in 
mofussil/remote areas to undergo CPE activities. With this aim, the CPE Committee proposed to open CPE 
POUs in all States/Districts/Tehsils in India to facilitate all members of the ICAI residing in far flung areas of 
the country for organisation of CPE programmes and for helping/aiding the members in mofussil/remote areas 
to undergo CPE activities in their jurisdiction areas. In this regard, the Committee researched on the data of 
ICAI Members and identified the possibility of opening new CPE Study Chapters & Study Groups as CPE 
POUs in all Districts/Tehsils in India and accordingly informed and invited all the ICAI Members District-wise 
with a request to identify and inform the other areas where CPE POUs (CPE Study Chapters and Study Groups) 
may be opened. 


e Members feedback on CPE Mechanism and implementation 


Recognizing the importance of Continuous Professional Education (CPE) in a rapidly changing environment, 
the CPE Committee is committed to supporting members' professional growth. To improve CPE guidelines and 
delivery, an online feedback form has been introduced to gather members’ experiences, preferences, and 
suggestions. This input will help tailor the CPE framework to better meet members’ needs and enhance the 
overall effectiveness of the program.

e Re-constitution of CPE Regional Monitoring Committee (RMC) in all five Regions for the Council 
year 2025-26 


For 2025-26, the CPE Committee has reconstituted Regional Monitoring Committees (RMCs) in all five 
regions to oversee CPE activities. Their responsibilities include reviewing monthly reports and attendance on 
the CPE Portal, addressing issues faced by CPE units, monitoring the functioning of study chapters and circles, 
nominating monitors, collecting and compiling participant feedback, and submitting quarterly reports. RMCs 
are also required to meet at least once every quarter and report their proceedings to the CPE Committee.

7.0 Women & Members Excellence Committee (WMEC) 


As a true partner in nation building, ICAI has setup the Women & Young Members Excellence Committee 
(erstwhile Women Members Excellence Committee) which is a non-standing Committee of ICAI formed under 
regulatory provisions of Chartered Accountants Act, 949. With the inclusion of Young members within the ambit 
of the Committee, the Committee has widened its scope to effectively work towards excellence and upskilling of 
both women & young member in the dynamic and challenging work environment. WYMEC especially work 
towards promoting the fulfilment of Women and young Members’ potential through capacity building initiatives, 
skill development activities, providing platform for professional and employment opportunities.

8. OTHER COMMITTEES/BOARDS 
8.l Audit Committee 


The Audit Committee of the Institute was established in April 200l by the Council as a non-standing committee 
with a clearly defined mandate. Since 2009, it has been chaired exclusively by a Government Nominee to ensure 
greater independence. To further enhance its autonomy, members of the Executive Committee and Finance 
Committee are not permitted to serve on the Central Audit Committee. Additionally, five Regional Audit 
Committees—Southern, Western, Central, Northern, and Eastern—support the Committee’s work, ensuring 
regional representation and effective oversight. 


Functions 


The Committee is responsible for overseeing the financial reporting process and ensuring the accuracy, integrity, 
and transparency of the Institute’s financial disclosures. It reviews audit reports, discusses observations with 
auditors, recommends corrective actions, and strives to strengthen the internal control environment. The Committee 
remains committed to good governance and continuous improvement in audit practices. 


Statutory Audit 


e Appointment of Statutory Auditors- In accordance with Section |8(5) of the Chartered Accountants 
Act, 949, the statutory auditors for ICAI’s Branches, Regional Councils, Decentralised Offices, Centre of 
Excellence, and Head Office are appointed from a panel of two firms recommended by the Comptroller and 
Auditor General (C&AG) of India, effective from FY 2022-23. This system ensures continuity and avoids 
audit delays. A status report on these appointments is regularly shared with the C&AG. 


e Audit Reporting Framework- The statutory auditors’ reporting framework is governed by Regulations 
96 and 97 of the Chartered Accountants Regulations, 988. 


e Joint Statutory Auditors- The accounts of the ICAI Head Office are audited by two joint statutory 
auditors, bringing diverse expertise and ensuring comprehensive review and accountability. 


Internal Audit 


e Internal Audit Coverage- A robust internal audit mechanism is in place for all major units including 
branches with over a thousand members, Regional Councils, Decentralised Offices, the Centre of 


[भाग ता--खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 259 


Excellence and the Head Office. The internal audit is conducted under the supervision of the Audit 
Committee, which ensures transparency and auditor independence. 


e Appointment through Eol- Internal auditors are appointed through a transparent process involving an 
open invitation for Expressions of Interest (50) from CA firms. Selection is based on an objective 
evaluation and ranking system. Audits are conducted biannually and cover both financial and compliance 
aspects, as per the prescribed scope and reporting format. Audit reports are reviewed by the respective 
Regional or Central Audit Committees for follow-up action. 


Annual Accounts 


e Unmodified Audit Opinions- The Institute has consistently received unmodified (unqualified) audit 
opinions, reflecting sound financial management, robust internal controls, and adherence to high governance 
standards. 


e _ Financial Statement Format- ICAI prepares its financial statements in accordance with the illustrative 
format for Not-for-Profit Organizations, as per the Technical Guide issued by the Institute. The format is 
customized to enhance relevance and clarity for stakeholders. 


e Approval Process- The approval of audited financial statements follows a structured and statutory 
process under Section 8(5A) of the Chartered Accountants Act, 949, and Regulation 200 of the Chartered 
Accountants Regulations, 988: 


> Draft accounts are reviewed by the Finance Committee and submitted to the Management Committee. 
The Management Committee evaluates and forwards them to the Audit Committee. 
The Audit Committee reviews and submits the accounts to the Council. 


The Council sends the accounts to the statutory auditors. 


VV ४ WV 


Post-audit, the report is circulated among Council members. 
> The Council finally approves the accounts and ensures their publication in the Gazette of India. 
8.2 Committee for Members in Entrepreneurship and Public Services (CME&PS) 


The Committee for Members in Entrepreneurship and Public Service (CMEPS) acts as an important link between ICAI 
leadership and members engaged in public service or entrepreneurship. With a focus on promoting the Public Service 
and Entrepreneurship as career option for CAs, the Committee undertakes various initiatives to inspire and empower 
members. Many Chartered Accountants currently serve in senior roles across government departments, ministries, 
legislatures, judiciary, regulatory bodies, and entrepreneurial ventures and actively contributing to governance, 
economic growth, and the nation’s development. The Committee organizes Residential Meets/ Interactive Meets of 
ICAI members in Public Service with the objective of soliciting suggestions of ICAI Members in Public Service to 
identify matters of National importance and Committee is continuously exploring the various opportunities that lies in 
Entrepreneurship for its CA members. To encourage aspiring CAs in both fields, the Committee regularly conducts 
mentorship sessions, orientation and training programmes, webinars, seminars, and regional meets. These initiatives 
aim to offer guidance, build capacity, and develop an entrepreneurial culture while supporting members in contributing 
to nation building.

8.4 Committee on Public and Government Financial Management (CP&GFM) 


The ICAI in line with its mission and vision, constituted the Committee on Public & Government Financial 
Management (CPGFM) to improve accounting, financial reporting and management in all tiers of Government in 
India including local bodies. Apart from formulating Accounting Standards for Local Bodies (ASLBs), the 
Committee focuses on capacity building of the accounts/ finance staff of various tiers of Government by several 
means such as Training Programmes, Webinars, e-learning modules, etc. The Committee also runs Certificate 
Course on Public Finance & Government Accounting that can be attended by officials of Government & 
Autonomous bodies. In addition, CPGFM provides technical and administrative support for the Certificate Course 
for Accountants of Panchayats and Municipal Bodies (.९., a joint initiative of ICAI and O/o C&AG of India) being 
run through Board for Local Bodies Accountants Certification (BLoAC) established under ICAI Accounting 
Research Foundation (ICAI-ARF). This initiative reflects ICAI’s commitment to nation building by extending the 
professional expertise of Chartered Accountants beyond the corporate sector to the public at large.

8.5 Editorial Board 


The Editorial Board is a specialized non-standing committee of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
(ICAI) dedicated to the mission of consistently providing members with professional knowledge and relevant 
matters through the journal, The Chartered Accountant. This journal empowers members by enhancing their 
professional knowledge and enjoys immense value among its readers, with a circulation exceeding 400,000, 
including both e-journal and printed copies."The Chartered Accountant" journal is a flagship publication of ICAI, 
showcasing the Institute’s thought leadership and strengthening its brand presence among members, students, and 
stakeholders. Curated by the Editorial Board, the journal serves as a source of insights—delivering cutting-edge 
developments, expert perspectives, and emerging trends in the accounting profession. With a focus on continuous 
learning and professional excellence, it plays a vital role in connecting the ICAI community with the evolving 
landscape of finance, governance, and global best practices. 


Initiatives towards Developing Nation 


Through the monthly journal The Chartered Accountant, the Editorial Board has played a pivotal role in nation- 
building by empowering ICAI members with cutting-edge knowledge, global perspectives, and evolving 


268 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SECc.4] 


professional practices. By consistently introducing evolving and contemporary trends and advancing thought 
leadership, the Board is deeply committed to shaping a future-ready accounting profession that contributes 
meaningfully to India’s economic growth and global standing. 


Several significant initiatives in this direction include the following: 
(0) Knowledge Enrichment through Articles: 


During the period, The Chartered Accountant journal featured a wide array of articles covering diverse and 
contemporary topics relevant to the accounting profession. In addition to its regular sections of professional 
interest, the journal published special issues aimed at enriching members' knowledge on critical and emerging 
subjects. These included focused editions on India — Global Hub for Accountancy Profession, Leadership, Public 
Finance, Artificial Intelligence, MSMEs, Sustainability, and other key technical domains, to keep its members 
well-informed and future-ready.

(ID) Qualitative coverage in The Chartered Accountant Journal:

coordination with various ICAI Committees. 


July 2024 Issue brought Out as Special Edition 


The July 2023 issue of the ICAI Journal was released as a Collector’s Edition to commemorate 75 Years of ICAI’s 
Excellence, aligned with the Inspiring India@00 vision. Celebrating ICAI’s legacy, the special edition featured 
the Institute’s history, contributions to nation-building, and included notable articles by the President of IFAC and 
Chair of IESBA. The issue also carried inspirational CA Day messages from 32 eminent dignitaries, including the 
President of India, several Governors, Union Ministers, Chief Ministers, and other key officials. A special segment 
titled "Journey of Trust" highlighted ICAI’s international presence, historical milestones such as the struggle for 
the 'Chartered' designation, ICAI stamps and logos, and iconic quotes, including a speech by India’s first President. 
The cover page symbolized ICAI’s pivotal role over 75 years in shaping the profession and contributing to the 
vision of Building New India.

8.6 Infrastructure Development Committee (IDC) 


In the year 204, Infrastructure Development Committee was formed as a non-standing Committee of the Institute. 
Since 204, the ICAI has a robust infrastructure policy in place, which ensures financial prudence and discipline. 
This year, Committee has modified the Infrastructure Policy for Branches and Regional Councils/Offices. The 
policy defines what all facilities can be provided, composition of local Infrastructure Committees, policy and 
procedure for acquisition of land/ building, indicative area, permissible grant from Head Office, powers and 
delegation vested with various authorities within the Institute. Since the policy itself defines the financial powers, 
all infrastructure projects from the year 20l4 onwards are being approved by IDC, instead of the Finance 
Committee. Since formulation of Infrastructure policy, the ICAI has initiated following projects:

8.7 


International Affairs Committee (IAC) 


(D Initiatives of IAC for recognition of professional opportunities abroad 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has established Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) 
with 8 international professional bodies to facilitate mutual recognition of accountancy qualifications. These 
include CPA Australia, CAANZ (under renewal), SAICA(under renewal), CPA Canada(under renewal), MICPA, 
CPA Ireland, ICAEW, and ICAN. Agreements with CAANZ, SAICA, and CPA Canada are currently under 


renewal 


e Renewal of MRA with CPA Ireland 


In view of the amalgamation of CPA Ireland with the Chartered Accountants Ireland on September 0, 2024, 
after which the identity of CPA Ireland shall cease to exist but the new institute assures respect for existing 
reciprocity agreements, ICAI and CPA Ireland have progressed with their arrangements for the benefit of the 


members at either end. 


e Signing of Addendum with CA ANZ 


ICAI and CA ANZ previously had a reciprocity membership agreement. During the year, both the organizations 
actively engaged for review of course curriculum of each other and pending final review extended arrangement 
through an addendum for the benefit of the members. 


270 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


e Benchmarking of ICAI qualification by Ecctis 


To enhance global opportunities for its members, ICAI engaged Ecctis in 209 to benchmark its qualifications 
against UK and UAE education standards. The study found ICAI’s Intermediate level equivalent to a Bachelor's 
degree and the Final level equivalent to a Master's degree. Due to recent curriculum updates, ICAI has initiated 
a fresh evaluation with Ecctis to reaffirm its international standing, benefiting members seeking professional 
opportunities abroad. 


e Awareness sessions with MRA Partner 


ICAI has been actively promoting Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) with global partners to create 
overseas opportunities for its members. During the reported period, ICAI organized 5 awareness sessions with 
CPA Australia across major cities and regions in India through both physical and virtual formats. Additionally, 
6 awareness sessions were conducted with ICAEW in key cities nationwide, also via hybrid modes. ICAI also 
held a virtual awareness session with CPA Ontario, reaching a broad network of members and stakeholders to 
enhance understanding and engagement with international MRA opportunities. 


(ता) Globalizing ICAI’s Brand Equity 
World Forum of Accountants- A resounding success 


ICAI organized the inaugural World Forum of Accountants (WOFA) from January 3] to February 2, 2025, at 
Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, aiming to position India as a global hub for finance and accounting. The landmark event 
gathered over 6,500 delegates from 32 countries and prominent global accounting bodies such as ICAEW, CPA 
Australia, CPA Canada, and SAFA, with an additional 800 participants attending virtually. Centered around the 
theme "Accountability Meets Innovation (AI): For a Sustainable Planet," the forum explored the integration of 
financial integrity, technology, and sustainability. WOFA featured l0 special sessions, 22 concurrent sessions, and 
4 panel discussions addressed by over 200 international and national thought leaders. The event included 67 
sponsors & exhibitors, 27 Indian firms, and an ICAI pavilion showcasing various committee initiatives. 
Additionally, SAFA Committee and Board Strategy Meetings, and bilateral meetings with CPA Australia, CPA 
Canada, and CA Maldives were held on the sidelines, reinforcing ICAI’s global engagement and leadership in the 
profession.

e Enhancing Brand CA Globally through ICAI Overseas Chapters & Representative Offices 


ICAI has always been working untiringly in the direction of effectively and efficiently serving its members 
based in overseas. ICAI has now 54 Chapters and 3] Representative offices in 85 global cities in 47 Countries 
aiding to positioning the ‘CA India’ as a ‘Brand’ worldwide for generating more professional avenues for 
Indian Chartered Accountants. During the period under report, ICAI has inaugurated 4 Chapters in Florida, 
Zurich, Los Angeles and Atlanta. These Chapters are our brand Ambassadors and they uphold the mission of 
Indian Chartered Accountancy high in foreign soil. Representative office in Rotterdam in Netherlands and 
Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, Tennessee, and San Diego in USA were also launched. Representative offices 
abroad are opened where currently ICAI Chapters cannot be formed thus bringing together ICAI members 
abroad and enabling effective reach and service to its members, thus aiding to positioning the Brand “Indian 
CA” worldwide for generating more professional avenues for Indian Chartered Accountants. 


e Mobile App “Diaspora” for ICAI Overseas Members 


On October 25, 2024, ICAI launched the Android and iOS versions of its "Diaspora" mobile app to better 
connect with its international community of around 4,000 overseas members. The launch occurred during an 
event of the Toronto Chapter, coinciding with then-President CA Ranjeet Kumar Agarwal’s visit to New York, 
San Francisco, and Toronto. The app provides members with easy access to information, enhances engagement, 
and fosters networking. It also synchronizes with ICAI’s central database to identify members who have not 
updated their overseas professional addresses, improving the accuracy of membership records. 


e New Website of International Affairs Committee 


ICAI launched a separate website of the International Affairs Committee to enhance communication, foster 
collaboration, and provide a central hub for information and resources on August 5, 2024 coinciding with the 
visit of the then President CA. Ranjeet Kumar Agarwal to Australia. Recognizing the increasing importance of 
digital platforms in international affairs, the website aims to bridge geographical gaps, facilitate knowledge 
sharing among members and stakeholders, and promote transparency and accessibility to committee activities 
and initiatives. 


e Directions of the Council for Accreditation and Functioning of Chapters Outside India 


ICAI developed a comprehensive guidelines “Directions of the Council for Accreditation and Functioning of 
Chapters Outside India” for strengthening ICAI overseas Chapters in order to serve the members abroad in an 
effective and efficient way. 


e ICAI Best Oversesa Chapter Awards 2024 


Since 203, the International Affairs Committee (IAC) has annually presented the ICAI Best Chapter Awards 
to recognize overseas Chapters for their outstanding efforts in promoting the ‘Indian CA’ brand and fostering 
member networking abroad. The awards honor Chapters’ exemplary achievements in advancing the Chartered

during ICAI’s 75" Annual Day function held on February 2, coinciding with the World Forum of Accountants.

8.8 Management Committee 


Management Committee, constituted in 20I5 as non-standing Committee of the Council, is mandated to consider 
matters pertaining to formation of Branches, setting up of Chapters abroad, MoUs/ MRAs with national/ 
international bodies, appointment of central auditors of ICAI, annual accounts of the Institute, matters referred by 
the Central Government and other regulatory bodies, proposals for amendments in the Chartered Accountants Act, 
949, Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, Regional Councils and Branches matters, Members/CA 
firms/LLPs/mergers/demergers/networking related matters and proposals received from other 
committees/departments of the Institute having administrative and policy implications and making its 
recommendations to the Council wherever required. 


8.9 Public Relations Committee (PRC) 


The Public Relations Committee has been working towards strengthen and enhance the brand image of the ICAI as 
a premier accountancy body and the sole regulatory authority for the profession of Chartered Accountancy in India 
through various ways and means, as considered appropriate within the framework of the CA Act. The PR 
Committee further endeavors to foster good relationship with Media and other Stakeholders in coordination with 
various committees of ICAI to provide smooth communication, information and to enhance the visibility of ICAI. 
Media serves as one of the most strategic tools for effectively conveying opinions and perspectives to the public, 
policymakers, and key stakeholders. In recent times, ICAI has proactively leveraged the media to communicate its 
views and decisions with clarity and impact. The Public Relations Committee has not only expanded ICAI’s media 
footprint in terms of reach and volume but has also built meaningful long-term relationships with key national 
media.

8.0 Research Committee 


The Research Committee of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, established in 955, is one of the 
oldest technical committees dedicated to fostering a strong research culture to enhance professional services. Its 
primary objective is to conduct research and strengthen institutional capacity in accounting and allied fields for the 
benefit of the profession and the nation. The Committee actively promotes research and innovation through various 
projects, programs, workshops, and seminars. It also focuses on developing strategies for global collaboration in 
key areas of international importance. The Committee conducts research on diverse areas such as the profession, 
economy, education, business, industry, health, and infrastructure. It provides research-based insights to support 
government policy, offers recommendations, and prepares representations on accounting and professional matters. 
Focused on promoting high-quality research, it leads strategic initiatives to improve financial reporting and offers 
thought leadership on emerging trends and best practices affecting the profession.

8.] Strategy, Perspective Planning and Monitoring Committee (SPP&MC) 


The Strategy Perspective Planning and Monitoring Committee is a non-standing committee of the Institute of 
Chartered Accountants of India (ICAJ) serves a critical role in shaping long-term ICAI Vision and objectives. The 
primary purpose of this committee is to engage in strategic planning, ensuring that the ICAI develops and 
implements effective strategies to meet its goal. The committee is committed to effective risk management, 
identifying potential challenges, and adapting strategies to navigate a dynamic business environment. By analysing 
various perspective, trends and factors, the committee aim to provide a comprehensive outlook for the 
organization’s future. Additionally, it plays a critical role in monitoring the execution of strategic initiatives, 
assessing their impact, and making adjustments as necessary. 


Activities/Initiatives: 
(I Preparation of ICAI Vision 2049-Collaboration with IMA 


In pursuit of a forward-looking strategy for the Institute, the ICAI initiated the development of JCAI Vision 2049 
through a collaborative engagement with the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA). This 
collaboration aims to outline a comprehensive roadmap that aligns the Institute’s long-term goals with emerging 
global, technological, and regulatory trends. 


(ID) Formation of Group for Preparation of the Vision Document 


Pursuant to the decision of the competent authority, a dedicated Group was constituted under the aegis of the 
Strategy, Perspective Planning and Monitoring Committee (SPPMC) for the preparation of the Vision document. 


(IID) Submission of Revised Draft 


Inputs were sought by the IIMA via conducting series of interaction with President, Vice President, Central Council 
Members, Secretary, Faculty, Boards of Studies, senior officers and members of ICAI for preparation of ICAI 
Vision 2049. Draft questionnaires were circulated to seek views of members, students, present and past Council 
Members, and employees. A meeting of past Presidents was held on 2% March, 2024 at Jaipur to seek their views 
on ICAI Vision 2049. The views expressed therein were collated and placed before the SPPMC at its 0™ meeting 
held on 6"* April 2024 at New Delhi. Further, a meeting with past Council members was held on 27" April, 2024 
at New Delhi. The views expressed therein were also collated. With the approval of President, the summary of 
responses received on questionnaire, summarisation of views expressed by past Presidents, present Council 
members and past council members had been shared with IIMA on 3" May 2024. IIMA thereafter submitted their 
first draft to SPPMC on for its consideration on 5" June 2024. The same was considered by the Group wherein all 
members of the Council were invited. The members therein made certain suggestions for improvement in the draft 
Vision Document which were communicated to IIMA on 2 June, 2024. 


Subsequently, IIMA submitted the second draft report via email dated 25" June 2024. The revised draft was 
acknowledged by the office, and further discussions were held regarding the structure and content of the Vision 
2049 Document. In addition, some further observations have been communicated to IIMA for inclusion in the final 
version. IIMA has agreed to incorporate these inputs and will submit the final report shortly, along with a concise 
5-6 page Vision Document aligned with the structure and format of the ICAI Vision 2030. The final Vision 2049 
document will serve as a strategic blueprint to guide ICAI’s evolution over the next 25 years, reinforcing its role as 
a global leader in the accounting profession. Vision 2049 will mark a significant milestone in shaping ICAI’s future 
trajectory with clarity, purpose, and strategic foresight.

8.3 Right to Information Act, 2005 


The basic objective of the Right to Information Act is to empower the citizens, to acclaim transparency and 
accountability in the working of every public authority. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) a 
statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament i.e. The Chartered Accountants Act, 949 is a public authority as 
envisaged under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act,2005. In compliance of the provisions of the RTI Act, 2005 and 
direction of the Central Information Commission, officers of the Institute have been designated as Central Public 
Information Officer, Central Assistant Public Information Officer, First Appellate Authority (FAA). A large number 
of RTIs is being received by RTI Cell, ICAI from the students, members, other stakeholders & citizens and the 
same have been responded. 


Disclosure under Section 4() (b) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 


Further, in terms of the Section 4()(b) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, necessary disclosures have been 
made by the Institute by hosting them on the website of the Institute www.icai.org and the same are updated from 
time to time. During the period 2024-25, it is to note that total 2,29,38] (two lakh twenty nine thousand and three 
hundred eighty-one) applications have been received which include the applications requesting for certified copies (
